cardinality.instructions: For this verified original mutation/cohort workflow, choose final-net A or ordered-stage B as the least complex complete committed-model source semantics. Compare the same edge cases and requirements, including transaction-local create/remove and repeated updates; distinguish durable stage history from stored record commits.

criteria.A: Final-net proposal: one source per final stored record change, with actual final version and create/update/delete classification. Transaction-local create→remove emits none; existing update→remove emits one delete; repeated updates emit one final update. Preserve ordered history and explicit effects separately. Every emitted source retains full atomic routes/cut/receipt and immutable payload/current-state later guards. Aligns notifications with net stored changes, but suppresses intermediate authored stage notifications.
criteria.B: Ordered-stage proposal: one source per successful ordered business mutation stage in the winning history, preserving stage model/change/reserved version/attribution. Create→remove emits create and delete despite no final live row; repeated updates emit distinct occurrences. All routes/cuts/receipts still share original fence/final provisional cutoff. Payloads contain identities only; later bodies load current state without resurrecting intermediate rows. Preserves transition notifications, but increases sources/cuts and must distinguish historical stages from net stored commits.
